Animal Travel Desk Intake and Handling

The main rule is simple: every animal travel request must be handled with calm, humane care, and every passenger must get clear service in a steady tone. Staff are expected to listen first, then check the travel details, then explain the next step without pressure. When a passenger arrives worried about a pet, the desk should slow the pace, keep the exchange respectful, and route the concern to the supervisor if the issue needs review. The desk also keeps safety in view at all times, so any sign of distress, escape risk, or unsafe crate condition must be acted on at once.

For reptile travel, <<FACT F060>> staff must follow the same quiet standard of care used for all live animal handling. The animal should be treated gently, the carrier should remain secure, and the record should be complete before the passenger moves on. If a handler sees a hazard, the handler must stop and bring in the safety coordinator for review. The coordinator checks the condition, explains the prevention step, and confirms that the handling plan stays within company practice.

The desk welcomes questions in a warm professional tone, and it should never sound hurried or dismissive. If a traveler needs help understanding an animal-related rule, the reply should stay direct, brief, and useful. Supervisors are expected to listen carefully when a passenger is worried, because careful listening often prevents mistakes later in the process. Staff should not improvise around animal care or promise a result that has not been checked. Instead, they should use the current guidance, record the action taken, and keep the customer informed in plain language.

This section applies to all Companion Animal Travel Desk work at Aurelia Skyways, and any unclear case should be sent to the supervisor or the safety coordinator for review.
